summary: API Gateway 5xx wave during scheduler batch-coalescing glitch
description: Issue summary: Customers reported a sudden increase in 5xx responses and long tail latency for chat and embedding routes. Impact: LyraSearch (enterprise) saw elevated error rates (5xx) across mixed chat+embedding traffic for ~18 minutes during morning traffic ramp. Environment: prod us-east-1, hosted API, dedicated route for LyraSearch.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send concurrent mixed requests: 1000 short-chat requests (streaming) + 500 embedding uploads in 1 minute against tenant route
2) Observe API Gateway spike in 502/503/504 and increased backend timeouts
3) Check scheduler metrics for batch-coalescing latency and runtime preemption events
observed_behavior: - API Gateway returning 502/503/504 ~12% error-rate at peak
- Upstream serving-runtime showing rapid worker restarts and short-lived preemption signals
- Scheduler batch coalescer reported sudden 10x increase in coalescing latency leading to oversized batches
- Tracing shows hedged retries issued from API Gateway for requests exceeding 1s, amplifying backend load
expected_behavior: - Batch coalescing to respect max-batch-size and target latency budget
- No hedged-retry amplification under normal prewarm conditions
logs: [2026-03-12T09:05:14Z] runtime: worker pid=4821 SIGTERM preempt=true reason=gpu_rebalance
[2026-03-12T09:05:15Z] apigw: hedged_retry dispatched for request id=aa12ff (attempts=2)
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: increased batch coalescing latency produced oversized batches that triggered runtime memory pressure and preemption
Checked autoscaler and dedicated pool: no large scale-downs at the time; ephemeral rebalances observed due to NVML notifications
Found correlation between keystore rotation job (internal maintenance window) and spikes in accept-queue latency upstream of scheduler
Tracing shows a subset of long-lived streaming sessions holding sockets open, reducing concurrency headroom and delaying scheduler dispatch
timeline: 09:03 UTC - Customer begins high mixed workload (reported)
09:04 UTC - Keystore rotation job started in us-east maintenance window
09:05 UTC - Scheduler coalescer latency spikes, apigw 502/503 wave begins
09:10 UTC - Runtime workers restart intermittently, backpressure increases
09:21 UTC - Traffic declines, error rate returns to baseline
actions_taken: 1) Scoped the affected tenant routes and temporarily disabled hedged retries for tenant LyraSearch to avoid amplification (applied at 09:07)
2) Manually adjusted scheduler coalescer target latency to a lower threshold in us-east to force earlier dispatching of smaller batches (09:08)
3) Kicked a rolling restart of a subset of serving-runtime nodes showing NVML preemption anomalies (09:09)
4) Paused non-critical keystore rotation job mid-run after confirming correlation with accept-queue latency (09:11)
5) Notified LyraSearch and opened dedicated support bridge
resolution: Temporary mitigations applied: hedged retries disabled for tenant, scheduler coalescing tightened, keystore rotation paused. Error rate returned to baseline after mitigations and runtime restarts. Root cause under follow-up: race between keystore maintenance affecting socket handling and scheduler coalescer heuristics that allowed oversized batches under degraded accept-queue conditions.
next_steps: - Engineering to add a guard in coalescer to cap batch size if accept-queue latency > threshold
- Modify keystore rotation to use rolling low-impact mode during high-traffic windows (RFC underway)
- Add an alert for hedged-retry amplification patterns (APIGW -> runtime retry ratio > 1.5)
- Post-incident runbook update and a follow-up postmortem scheduled (owners: Scheduling team, Runtime team)
